principles: Resume mode is ADDITIVE to run-batch: the fresh-campaign path is byte-unchanged so M2 evidence + selfcheck-m2 stay valid.
Identity-keyed idempotent resume: skip iterationIds already recorded; reconcile the FINAL multiset (== protocol cross-product, 0 dup / 0 gap).
A mid-iteration casualty resolves to a stop record OR a clean re-run, never a silent half-record.
ONE driver is both the M2 campaign producer and the M3 resume target (evidence stays coherent).
resume-reconciliation.json is the H3 evidence; the probe kills DETERMINISTICALLY (boundary + crash hook).
drivers: run-batch is already append-only + identity-keyed but lacks resume; adding it is the H3 machinery.
The atomic-single-line append makes a pre-append kill a clean re-run; a mid-append kill needs trailing-line repair.
H3 is evaluable whenever the campaign ran; the reconciliation is mechanical (multiset compare).

options.name: add-resume-to-run-batch
pros: ONE coherent driver (M2 producer = M3 resume target)
Reuses the append-only + identity-key + strict guard
cons: Modifies an M2-DONE file (must keep M2 evidence valid)

options.name: separate-resumable-driver
cons: Duplicates the driver; the two can drift; the M3 evidence would not be about the same driver M2 proved

rationale: The plan wants resume-probe to restart THE replay driver; a separate resumable driver would drift from the M2-proven one and make the H3 evidence about a different driver. The resume mode is strictly additive so M2 batch-ledger.jsonl + selfcheck-m2 stay valid.

preMortem.trigger: the resume branch alters the empty-ledger flow or record content
preMortem.consequence: M2 batch-ledger.jsonl no longer reproduces / selfcheck-m2 breaks
preMortem.mitigation: gate resume strictly on --resume + a non-empty existing ledger; assert selfcheck-m2 still passes after the change

preMortem.scenario: Mid-append kill leaves a half-record the resume mis-parses
preMortem.trigger: a kill during the atomic-ish append writes a truncated JSONL line
preMortem.consequence: resume reads a malformed line -> crash or a phantom iterationId
preMortem.mitigation: resume repairs/ignores a truncated trailing line; the casualty iterationId then re-runs cleanly

preMortem.consequence: the strict exact-multiset guard fails (dup) -> H3 falsified spuriously
preMortem.mitigation: skip iterationIds already present (proof OR stop) before running; verify 0 dup in reconciliation
